problem.title: Groups of Six
problem.statement: Which number of tiles can be separated into groups of 6 with no tiles left over?
hints: A divisible total must leave remainder zero.

solutionSteps.title: Find a complete boundary
solutionSteps.body: The multiples of 6 near the choices are 30, 36, and 42. Only 36 appears, and 36 = 6 × 6 with no remainder.

validationMethods: direct division of every choice by 6
notes: Only 36 has remainder zero when divided by 6.

problem.title: Pack Tennis Balls
problem.statement: Fifty-two tennis balls are packed equally into boxes holding 4 balls each. How many full boxes are used, and how many balls remain?

solutionSteps.title: Form equal groups
solutionSteps.body: Since 4 × 13 = 52, thirteen full boxes use every ball and the remainder is zero.

validationMethods: direct calculation 52 divided by 4 equals 13 remainder 0
independent repeated-addition count of thirteen groups

problem.title: Read a Factor Fact

choices.label: D
choices.text: 7 is the remainder when 56 is divided by 8

hints: A divisor is the number doing the exact dividing.

solutionSteps.title: Use the product
solutionSteps.body: Because 56 = 8 × 7, dividing 56 by 8 gives a whole-number quotient and remainder zero. Thus 8 is a divisor of 56.

validationMethods: independent direct division 56 divided by 8 equals 7 remainder 0
notes: Only choice B has the relationship direction correct.

problem.title: What the Final Zero Guarantees
problem.statement: Which list contains every number among 2, 5, and 10 that divides 3270?
hints: Ten is divisible by each listed divisor.

solutionSteps.title: Use place value
solutionSteps.body: The final zero means 3270 consists of complete tens. Since each ten is divisible by 2, 5, and 10, all three divide 3270.

validationMethods: independent direct divisions give quotients 1635, 654, and 327
notes: All three listed divisors divide the number exactly.

problem.title: A Digit for Divisibility by Nine
problem.statement: The three-digit number 4A2 is divisible by 9. What is the digit A?

solutionSteps.title: Use the digit sum
solutionSteps.body: The digit sum is 4 + A + 2 = 6 + A, which ranges from 6 to 15. The only multiple of 9 in that range is 9, so A = 3.

notes: A = 3 is the unique digit solution.

problem.title: Two Divisibility Boundaries
problem.statement: What is the least whole number greater than 50 that is divisible by both 6 and 8?
hints: List multiples of 8 greater than 50 in order.
Test each list entry for divisibility by 6.

solutionSteps.title: Search in order
solutionSteps.body: The multiples of 8 above 50 begin 56, 64, and 72. The first two are not divisible by 6, while 72 = 6 × 12.

solutionSteps.title: Verify both conditions
solutionSteps.body: Also 72 = 8 × 9, so 72 is divisible by both 6 and 8 and no smaller candidate above 50 works.

validationMethods: ordered enumeration of multiples of 8 above 50
independent product checks 72 equals 6 times 12 and 8 times 9
notes: 72 is the exact least common divisible value above 50.
